checks.invariant: Every file mutation reachable from a GUI burst that can later re-execute must be captured by the burst's change tracking (gui_changes) or neutralized by stray-kill before a snapshot can persist it.
checks.result: The desktop template command is ['/usr/local/bin/agentbox-desktop-start'] (config.py:74), whose start script execs startxfce4 as uid 1001 desktop with HOME=/home/desktop (agentbox-desktop-start:13-14,30). /home/desktop is mode 700 owned by desktop (Dockerfile:28-30), so the burst principal (uid 1001, reachable via the run-2 N-1 xfce4-terminal path) can write /home/desktop/.config/autostart/*.desktop. workspace_manifest's find is scoped to {WORKSPACE} (/workspace) only (sandbox.py:499), so _close_gui_burst's diff_manifest (service.py:237-248) never records a write under /home/desktop. snapshot() docker-commits the whole container including /home/desktop (sandbox.py:478). restore() rebuilds from the committed image and re-runs tpl.command (sandbox.py:516-520), re-executing startxfce4 and any ~/.config/autostart entry as uid 1001 outside any burst. The re-executed process launches at container boot, so it is always present in the burst-open baseline and exempt from gui_strays (sandbox.py:216). Net: a GUI-burst write outside /workspace is invisible to gui_changes, survives into snapshots, and re-executes on restore/restart with no monitoring.

checks.invariant: gui_strays must stop a uid-1001 payload that an autostart entry launches after a restore/restart.
checks.result: sbx5 harness importing agentbox.sandbox (python3.13, no net/Docker). Confirmed (1) workspace_manifest's find is scoped to {WORKSPACE} with no /home component; (2) gui_strays([session, autostart-payload], window_pids=set(), baseline={1,100,200}) returns [] (payload survives) when the payload is present at burst open (the restart case, since autostart runs at boot before any burst), whereas the identical payload launched DURING the burst (baseline={1,100}) is returned [200] (killed). This demonstrates the baseline exemption that lets a re-executed autostart process evade stray-kill after restore/restart.

candidates.title: GUI-burst write to /home/desktop/.config/autostart escapes gui_changes/stray-kill, persists into snapshots, and re-executes as uid 1001 on restore/restart
candidates.description: A prompt-injected agent can drive the desktop GUI tools (the run-2 N-1 path that opens an xfce4-terminal as uid 1001 desktop) to write a Desktop Entry file at /home/desktop/.config/autostart/evil.desktop. This write lands outside /workspace, so it is never recorded by the GUI burst's gui_changes diff (which only scans /workspace), and the autostart file is inert on disk so the burst-close stray-kill (which only stops processes) does not remove it. When the control plane later docker-commits the container (AP-2 pre-snapshot before a destructive action, an interval GUI snapshot, or a manual/human snapshot), the autostart file is captured into the snapshot image. On a subsequent restore (human reverting to a 'clean' restore point) or restart, the desktop template re-runs its start script, which execs startxfce4 as uid 1001; XFCE session startup honours ~/.config/autostart, re-executing the attacker's Exec= command as the desktop user with a live X session, outside any GUI burst and with no gui_changes record. Because the re-executed process launches at container boot it is always inside the next burst-open baseline, so gui_strays exempts it from stray-kill. The result is attacker-controlled code that persists across snapshot/restore and silently re-arms itself, defeating the restore-point and GUI-burst monitoring the human relies on.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: GUI-burst change tracking (workspace_manifest/gui_changes) and the snapshot restore lifecycle scope file-mutation visibility to /workspace, but the desktop session's HOME (/home/desktop) is both writable by the burst principal (uid 1001) and re-executed at session start via ~/.config/autostart. No control captures, re-authorizes, or sanitizes /home/desktop between the burst, the docker commit, and the restore re-exec; and gui_strays structurally exempts any process present at burst open, which an autostart payload always is after a restart.

trace.description: Agent GUI tool (click/type/key) opens a burst and drives an xfce4-terminal as uid 1001 desktop (run-2 N-1); inside it the agent writes /home/desktop/.config/autostart/evil.desktop.
The burst manifest find is scoped to /workspace (-xdev), so a write under /home/desktop is outside scope and never enters the gui_changes diff computed in service.py:237-248.
The written .desktop file is not a process (stray-kill cannot touch it); after restore the autostart-launched process is present at burst open, so p['pid'] in baseline exempts it from the stray list.
docker commit captures the entire container filesystem including /home/desktop/.config/autostart, persisting the payload into the snapshot image.

Restore rebuilds from the committed image and re-runs tpl.command = /usr/local/bin/agentbox-desktop-start (config.py:74), which execs startxfce4 (agentbox-desktop-start:30); XFCE autostart re-executes the payload as uid 1001 with a live X session, outside any burst and unlogged.

evidence.description: workspace_manifest: find {WORKSPACE} -xdev ! -type d — manifest/gui_changes only ever covers /workspace, never /home/desktop.
_close_gui_burst computes diff_manifest(burst['manifest'], manifest) over the /workspace-only manifest, so writes outside /workspace produce no gui_changes record.
gui_strays: processes whose pid is in baseline are skipped; an autostart process launched at container boot is always in the burst-open baseline after restore/restart.
snapshot: c.commit(...) of the whole container captures /home/desktop including any autostart entry.
restore: _run_container(tpl, snaps[snap_id]['image'], ...) rebuilds from the committed image and re-runs the template command.
desktop Template command = ['/usr/local/bin/agentbox-desktop-start'], so restore/restart re-executes the XFCE start script.
Start script execs 'dbus-launch --exit-with-session startxfce4' as uid 1001 desktop with HOME=/home/desktop on every container start.
desktop user uid 1001 owns /home/desktop mode 700, so the burst principal can create ~/.config/autostart/*.desktop; it is in the agent group sharing /workspace.

blockers: Live desktop image fact: whether xfce4-session in agentbox-desktop:0.1 reads ~/.config/autostart (XDG_CONFIG_HOME default) and executes the Exec= line of a .desktop entry at session start. Standard XDG autostart behaviour, but image-specific and not source-visible; requires running the image.

Live control-plane fact: whether the agent's GUI tools can actually create /home/desktop/.config/autostart/evil.desktop via an xfce4-terminal as uid 1001 within a burst (run-2 N-1 is only partially mitigated). Requires the Docker-backed control plane.

Live Docker fact: whether docker commit + restore (sandbox.py:478,517) re-runs the start script from the committed image and thereby re-executes the autostart payload. Requires the Docker daemon; sbx5 has no Docker and no network.

validation_plan.local: Already performed in sbx5 (python3.13, no net/Docker, uid 65534, importing agentbox.sandbox from /target): harness agents/h-autostart/artifacts/h.out shows (1) workspace_manifest's find is scoped to {WORKSPACE} with no /home component, and (2) gui_strays returns [] for a uid-1001 payload present in the burst-open baseline (the restore/restart case) while returning [200] for the same payload launched during the burst — proving the baseline exemption and the /workspace-only change scope. The autostart re-execution step cannot be exercised locally because it needs the real desktop image.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on this host with Docker: (1) docker run --network none agentbox-desktop:0.1; as uid 1001 desktop write /home/desktop/.config/autostart/t.desktop with [Desktop Entry]/Type=Application/Exec=/bin/sh -c 'touch /home/desktop/PROOF_$(date +%s)'/X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true/Hidden=false. (2) docker commit the container to an image. (3) docker run that image with the same CMD (/usr/local/bin/agentbox-desktop-start) and, after startxfce4 comes up, check for /home/desktop/PROOF_* — its presence confirms autostart re-execution as uid 1001 on restore/restart. (4) Through the control plane: as an agent token, drive GUI tools to open xfce4-terminal and create the same autostart file, run a GUI burst to idle-close, and confirm no gui_changes event names /home/desktop; then take a snapshot and POST /sandboxes/{sid}/restore and confirm the payload ran and no gui_processes_stopped entry lists it. Use only dummy /home/desktop/PROOF_* markers; stop at first proof, do not extend to broader persistence.

hardening: images/desktop/agentbox-desktop-start:30 — startxfce4 re-runs ~/.config/autostart on every container start with no allowlist; consider setting GLib/XDG so the session ignores the per-user autostart dir, or chowning /home/desktop/.config/autostart to root and making it read-only to uid 1001.

agentbox/sandbox.py:499 — workspace_manifest/gui_changes only observes /workspace; the desktop user's writable HOME (/home/desktop) that is re-executed at session start is outside all burst monitoring. A manifest/snapshot-diff that also covers /home/desktop (at least .config/autostart, .bashrc, .config/xfce4, .config/sessions) would surface persistence writes.

agentbox/sandbox.py:216 — gui_strays unconditionally exempts baseline pids; a process whose executable/entry was introduced by a prior burst (e.g., an autostart file committed into the snapshot) is indistinguishable from a legitimate boot process after restore, so baseline membership is not a safe trust signal across restore boundaries.
